parole.testo: From Old Swedish kesar(e), keysar(e) (“emperor”), from Middle High German keiser, ultimately from Latin Caesar; the cognomen of Julius Caesar.

parole.significato: a magnet (piece of material that attracts metal by magnetism)
parole.testo: From Middle High German magnet(e), from Latin magnēs, from Ancient Greek μαγνης (magnēs, “Magnesian”).

From Middle High German sleier, sleiger, sloiger, slogier. Of uncertain ultimate origin, but most likely borrowed; perhaps related to Latin stragulus (“covering”). Compare Middle Low German sleyer, sloier, sloiger, Middle English scleire, scleyre, sleyre, slyre (“veil”).
